content: Plan: Forecaster -> Uncertainty <-> Critic (revision loop) -> Critic risk -> Planner.
Loaded 36,000 rows, 36 series, source=synthetic.
Goal: forecast demand 7 periods ahead for 36 series. Every sales-derived feature must be at least that old, otherwise the evaluation leaks the future.
Built 19 features; chronological split train < 2023-05-11, validation to 2023-08-03, test to 2023-09-27.
Trained hist_gbm model on 29,952 training rows.
Top demand drivers (permutation importance): roll_mean_28, price_rel, dow, item_code, temp_feat, is_event
Running the classical ETS baseline (rolling origin) over validation + test; it is both a benchmark and a blend candidate.
Held-out validation WAPE: gbm 0.279, blend 0.277, seasonal_naive 0.437, ets 0.323; blend weight on the model chosen on the calibration window = 0.8.
Using 'gbm' (validation WAPE 0.279; 36% lower than seasonal naive).
-> Uncertainty: 5,040 forecasts ready (validation + test).
Goal: 90% prediction intervals. Counts get noisier as demand grows, so residuals are scaled by sqrt(forecast+1) and calibrated per series with shrinkage to the global value.
Calibrated on 2,016 validation rows (the last 28 validation days are held back for the Critic).
-> Critic: Intervals ready. Please check coverage on the held-out validation window.
Coverage on the held-out validation window is 90.3% (target 90%); bias -4.2%.
Calibration approved: intervals are honest enough to drive safety stock.
Re-fitted the calibrator on the full validation window (3,024 rows) and applied interval scale x1.00.

Errors on consecutive days are correlated, so multi-period demand is more uncertain than independent daily sigmas suggest: the standardised error of P-period sums has std 1.07 on validation. Planner sigma will be inflated by x1.07.
Reliability scores computed per series (1 - validation WAPE). Least reliable: S3_I05, S2_I05, S3_I12.
-> Critic: Final intervals and sigma ready for shock assessment.

Three signals are checked for every series-period: (1) calendar events, (2) weather far outside the training climate for series that are weather-sensitive, in the direction that raises demand, (3) recent forecast errors that are worse than during validation. Each raises the risk multiplier.
Weather sensitivity learned from training data (pooled by item_id): 15 of 36 series (42%) react to temperature anomalies; only those can receive a weather flag.
Price signal: a price below 0.73 x its recent average is rarer than the 1% quantile of training prices and counts as a price shock.

Risk weights learned from validation errors and shrunk towards the hand-set priors: event 0.21 (prior 0.25, n=72), weather 0.29 (prior 0.35, n=45), price 0.17 (prior 0.20, n=15), drift 0.13 (prior 1.25, n=1306).
Test window: 7.1% of series-periods have an event flag, 9.7% a weather flag, 16.3% an error-drift flag, 0.2% a price flag; mean risk multiplier 1.07.
Risk multipliers published to the Uncertainty agent (interval widening) and the Planner (safety stock).
-> Uncertainty: Risk assessment complete; widen intervals on flagged days.
Widened intervals on Critic-flagged days (half-width x risk multiplier); 25.9% of test series-days affected.
-> Planner: Final risk-adjusted intervals published.
Adaptive conformal updating applied (gamma=0.15); mean test interval multiplier 1.07, max 2.01.

base_stock policy: order-up-to = expected demand over 3 periods (lead time 2 + review 1) plus z=1.64 x forecast std (95% target). Five policies are compared on the same test window as a ladder: classical -> better forecast -> calibrated uncertainty -> Critic risk -> nowcast correction, so each agent's contribution can be separated.

-> Orchestrator: Simulation and order recommendations complete.
Run complete. Outputs written to outputs/latest.
